speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Parliament is reopening at an important milestone in our history.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We have spent the last three years fighting the crisis of our generation.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Together, we found our way through the uncertainties and fears of the pandemic.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Because everyone played their part, we emerged stronger and more united than before.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Social capital amongst Singaporeans has deepened, trust in Government has strengthened and our global reputation has been enhanced.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: These strengths will prove crucial on the road ahead.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: But there are new challenges ahead, as we enter an increasingly dangerous and troubled world.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: The war in Ukraine rages on and is unlikely to end soon.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: How the crisis unfolds will have major implications for the security of countries everywhere.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Near-miss encounters are happening more frequently around the Taiwan Strait and South China Sea.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Neither side wants to go to war, but events have their own momentum and accidents can easily spiral out of control in ways no one can predict.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: The global order is also being reshaped by strategic geopolitical rivalry.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: The major powers are focused more on unilaterally securing their own advantage, than on promoting mutual interdependence or strengthening the multilateral system.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: The international norms that underpin peace and prosperity in the world are under severe strain.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: These are realities we have to adapt to.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: As a small nation, we must take the world as it is, not as we wish it to be.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: But we are far from powerless on the international stage by acting together with like-minded partners, both big and small.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We remain vigilant and proactive in defending ourselves against external threats.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We will continue to build a network of friends to advance our shared interests.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We will strive to preserve our sovereignty and the right to determine our own future, as we have done since Independence.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We will be subject to foreign influences and disinformation campaigns, aimed at shaping our domestic public opinion and pressing the Government to adopt certain positions.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We must do our utmost to resist such pressures.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We have to close ranks and stay united, regardless of race, religion, or political affiliation, especially when it comes to core national interests.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We must never allow external parties to divide us and should always stand together as one people to uphold Singapore’s vital interests.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Unity will also be important as we push forward against the economic headwinds.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Global trade and investment flows are facing growing obstacles.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Governments in the major economies are providing substantial fiscal support to develop strategic industries and strengthen their own industrial bases.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: This creates a more unlevel playing field and tougher competition for us.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We will adapt to these new circumstances and find opportunities amidst the challenges.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We cannot compete headto-head with big powers seeking to control key technologies and industries in the global economy.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: But we can be more agile and nimble than others, and respond more quickly and effectively to new challenges and opportunities.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We will run up against more binding constraints in land, labour and carbon over the coming years, and will have to do our best to manage them.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: But even as we adjust and adapt, a few fundamental imperatives will not change.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We must stay connected to the world, strengthen our connectivity infrastructure and entrench our position as a trusted and reliable business hub.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We must develop talents and skills of our people throughout their careers and continue to attract foreigners with entrepreneurial networks and expertise to help grow opportunities for Singaporeans.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We must invest in innovation to unlock new areas of growth, including in digitalisation and sustainability.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Importantly, we must nurture the strong tripartite partnership between Government, businesses and workers.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: If we are adaptable and resourceful, we can strengthen our competitive advantage, and position ourselves best to prosper and thrive in this new environment.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: To do well in this troubled world and remain one united people, we will need to strengthen our social fabric.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Every Singaporean must feel that they have a stake in our country.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: This exercise reaffirms the core values that we hold dear as Singaporeans: fairness, inclusivity, mutual support and the desire to give back to society.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We want every person to be treated equally with dignity and respect.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We want a Singapore where everyone belongs, and every citizen has the chance to achieve his or her fullest potential.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We want a society that values and supports families; where we care for and help one another and pitch in to make a difference to our community.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We will expand opportunities throughout life for every citizen, regardless of their starting points.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We will strengthen social safety nets so that in every stage of life, Singaporeans can better cope with uncertainties and look forward with confidence.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We will build a smart and liveable city – a green, connected and thriving metropolis that we are all proud to call home.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We will deepen Singaporeans’ sense of shared identity and mutual responsibility towards one another.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: These will be the key priorities for the remainder of this term of Government.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: First, we will expand opportunities throughout life for all, regardless of individual backgrounds and circumstances.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Meritocracy has long been the organising principle of our society.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: It has provided opportunities to countless Singaporeans with the drive and ability to excel.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: But as we prosper as a society, those who have already done well will naturally seek to pass on their advantages to their children.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: This is why absent major upheavals, all societies tend to become more stratified and less socially mobile over time.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We will do our utmost to combat this tendency.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We must not allow advantages and privileges to become entrenched and persist over generations.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We must ensure a broader and more open meritocracy that works well for all Singaporeans.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: This means rethinking our approach to education and work.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We will continue to prepare our children for the future, starting from their early years.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We will provide more resources to support those who start out with less.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: At the same time, we recognise the competitive stresses that have built up in our education system, especially amongst certain segments of society.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We will provide everyone with access to a good education, and many chances in life to learn and improve.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: But let us not be unwittingly drawn into an educational arms race and end up worse off as a society.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We must also re-examine how society rewards different skills and talents and recognises the full range of pathways to success.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We should accord greater value to those who are skilled with their hands and contribute through their technical and practical abilities, as well as those with the social and empathetic traits to excel in jobs, such as caregiving or community service.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Every Singaporean must have the opportunity to take on work they find fulfilling and meaningful, build on their talents, give of their best and be rewarded fairly for it.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: At the same time, we will step up support for the disadvantaged and vulnerable segments in our society.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We will uplift lower-income workers and families, and empower them to take the initiative to improve their own lives.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We will enhance support for persons with disabilities, so they can pursue their aspirations and participate fully as contributing members of society.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We will ensure that Singapore remains an open and inclusive society, where we uplift everyone with opportunities throughout their lives and where we interact with one another as equals, regardless of our backgrounds.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Second, in a world of rapid change, the Government will improve social safety nets to help Singaporeans better cope with disruptions and setbacks in life.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: With more uncertainty in the world economy and faster technological change, workers, especially those in their 40s and 50s, are at higher risk of skills obsolescence and unemployment.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Beyond helping displaced workers, we will further strengthen our SkillsFuture ecosystem to bring everyone along on our digitalisation and industry transformation journey.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We will enable every citizen to do a significant skills reboot in the course of their working lives.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: This will help to keep them employable, whether they progress further in their respective fields, or transit across to jobs in new areas of growth.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We will also strengthen the sense of assurance in other ways.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We will take better care of our growing number of seniors.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We will help Singaporeans enjoy their golden years with greater peace of mind, by enhancing retirement adequacy, and expanding care and living options.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We will enable more seniors to age in place, in the comfort of their own homes, with their families and friends close by.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We will also keep public housing affordable and accessible for Singaporeans.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Third, we will press on with longer-term efforts to build a city that is green, connected and highly liveable.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We will continue to renew and transform our urban landscape.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: New centres and districts will be developed outside of the Central Business District (CBD), to pilot creative urban solutions that transform the way our people live, work and play.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Technology will be a key enabler; our urban plans will be integrated with our Smart Nation vision.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Our built environment is not just about better hardware and infrastructure.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We will strengthen the distinctive cultures and heritages of different neighbourhoods.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We will have better-connected streets and green spaces that are conducive for walking and cycling, where people can meet, interact and connect with one another.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We will make our housing estates more vibrant spaces where children grow up together, where shared memories are formed and where we nurture our unique identity as a multi-racial and multi-religious nation.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Fourth, we will strengthen our collective responsibility to shape our new compact.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: More government action should not result in a greater sense of dependency and entitlement.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Instead, the Government will, through its actions, reinforce individual and family efforts, and bring forth contributions from other stakeholders.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: For instance, employers must do their part to invest in their workers.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Community partners must complement government efforts to support vulnerable families, just as we rallied to support one another through the pandemic.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Those who have done well must pay it forward and give others a hand, so that we help one another stand tall with dignity and pride.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: To tackle the complex challenges ahead, Singapore will need a stronger network of stakeholders to participate in nation building.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Committed businesses that champion socially responsible and sustainable practices.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: A passionate civil society that advocates for their visions of a better society.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: An active citizenry that takes ownership of issues.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: The Government will do more to mobilise and involve all stakeholders.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: In particular, our youths show strong interest to take action and initiate change on issues they care about, like mental well-being and sustainability.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We will engage the ideas, dynamism and energy of our young Singaporeans.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Ultimately, our refreshed social compact is about a shared understanding of how we relate to and support one another in our next phase of nationhood.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: By pooling our individual expertise, experiences and resources, we can achieve better outcomes for ourselves, our fellow citizens and our nation, Singapore.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Even as we focus on our present needs, we must also plan for the future and think on behalf of generations to come.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We are here today only because of what previous generations of Singaporeans did.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: They were willing to work hard and make sacrifices, to give us – their children and grandchildren – a better life.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We must uphold these same values and leave behind a Singapore that is better than the one today, for the sake of future generations.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Throughout our nation building journey, we have repeatedly faced challenges and setbacks.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: When we started out in 1965, the journey looked so daunting, with so many problems to solve.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: But with courage and determination, our founding leaders and pioneer generations tackled challenges head-on, one by one, and built this thriving metropolis.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We are now in a much stronger position – better poised to overcome our vulnerabilities and armed with crucial resources to push forward with confidence, however stormy the weather.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Our collective experiences have strengthened the mutual trust between Singaporeans and their confidence in our system of government.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: This virtuous circle relies on us partnering one another and working together to make the impossible, possible.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: They must continue to strengthen their bonds with Singaporeans, and work closely with them to write the next chapter of our Singapore Story.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: The trust between our political leadership and people, and between Singaporeans themselves, is a key strength we must continue to nurture and cherish.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: In so many societies, this has gone wrong.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: These societies face deep divides that are difficult to bridge.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Instead of bringing people together, political parties aggravate rifts by divisive appeals for support from competing groups.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Consequently, trust in government and its institutions plummets, making recovery even harder.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We cannot afford to let this happen in Singapore.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: In an open, diverse society, people will always have different views.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: But our conversations also must be constructive, respectful and responsible, based on facts and sound analysis.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Our interactions with one another must be anchored on mutual respect and trust, and a shared goal of advancing the larger public interest.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: In this way, we can work through our differences, enlarge our common ground and draw strength from our diverse perspectives.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Out of our diversity, we have built a deep reservoir of social capital and trust.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: As we commemorate the centenary of Mr Lee Kuan Yew’s birth, we should reflect on the values and principles of the founding generation of leaders.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We should reaffirm and uphold our shared values, while re-examining what needs to be updated and possessing the courage to break new ground.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Only then can we forge ahead confidently, firm in our footing and sure of our destination.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: ADDENDA TO THE PRESIDENT'S ADDRESS AT THE OPENING OF THE SECOND SESSION OF THE FOURTEENTH PARLIAMENT ON MONDAY, 10 APRIL 2023
